raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

- Add a LoRA-scoped `use_transformer_engine_op_fuser` switch so PEFT can opt into Transformer Engine fusion without changing the model-wide fusion setting.
- Preserve the original expert linear forward and fuse the LoRA output projection into its output, avoiding a second base-weight GEMM for supported non-grouped expert linears at TP1.
- Keep grouped expert adapters and TP>1 on the existing fallback path, with dispatch and forward/backward parity coverage.

## B300 before / after

Benchmark-only capacity screen on Nemotron Lightning: one B300 node, exact 131,041-token packed sequence, TP1/DP4, recompute r2, one logical forward request across four ranks.

| Candidate | Terminal point | Terminal allocation | Completed calls |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Main-qualified baseline, XID 1052895 | First shared-expert FC1 base GEMM | 928 MiB requested, about 215 MiB free | 0 forward / 0 backward / 0 optimizer |
| Tuned candidate, XID 1052959 | Passed MoE; failed later in attention projection | 672 MiB requested, 114.81 MiB free | 0 forward / 0 backward / 0 optimizer |

The tuned candidate also used 32-way MLP chunking, so this is end-to-end progress evidence rather than an isolated kernel speedup. Neither run completed a forward pass, so throughput and speedup are not claimed. The live image used the equivalent expert-merge implementation from Bridge commit `9379a8492f9cdfcf808a7f56fc3004565381a74b`; this PR rebases the focused change onto current `main`.

## Testing

- `pre-commit run --all-files`
- CUDA 13 container: `python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/peft/test_lora.py -q -k "lora_initialization or lora_op_fuser"` (4 passed); GPU parity test added for CI hardware

@@ -349,6 +349,43 @@ def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, None]:
         return out, None
 
 
+class TEFusedLoRAMergeLinear(TEFusedLoRALinear):
+    """Fuse the LoRA output projection into an existing base-linear output."""
+
+    def __init__(self, to_wrap: nn.Module, adapter: nn.Module):
+        super().__init__(to_wrap, adapter)
+        self._fused_lora_branches: Optional[tuple[te.ops.Sequential]] = None
+
+    def _make_fused_lora_branch(self) -> te.ops.Sequential:
+        """Construct the LoRA branch without rebuilding the base linear."""
+        return self._make_lora_branch(
+            in_features=self.adapter.linear_in.weight.size(1),
+            out_features=self.adapter.linear_out.weight.size(0),
+            tensor_parallel_mode=None,
+            tensor_parallel_group=None,
+            sequence_parallel=False,
+            accumulate_into_main_grad=False,
+        )
+
+    def forward(
+        self, x: torch.Tensor, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any
+    ) -> torch.Tensor | tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor | None]:
+        """Run the base linear, then fuse the LoRA B GEMM into its output."""
+        if not self._adapter_enabled:
+            return LoRALinear.forward(self, x, *args, **kwargs)
+
+        linear_output, bias, layernorm_output = self.base_linear_forward(x, *args, **kwargs)
+        if self._fused_lora_branches is None:
+            # A tuple avoids registering the fused view of the adapter weights as another submodule.
+            self._fused_lora_branches = (self._make_fused_lora_branch(),)
+
+        with te.fp8_autocast(enabled=False):
+            combined = self._fused_lora_branches[0](layernorm_output.contiguous(), linear_output)
+        if not self._base_returns_tuple:
+            return combined
+        return combined, bias
+
